notes:
Account summary:
- Company: Sagehaven Inference Labs — research arm of a mid-sized pharmaceutical group. Heavy regulation around PHI/PII, prefer EU-only data residency.
- Primary asks: private VPC deployment with customer-managed KMS, full audit logging, and strict retention controls.
- Workloads: batch & online embeddings for de-identified clinical notes, doc search for internal R&D, and a low-latency QA assistant for internal trials.

Technical / architecture fit notes:
- Topology preference: multi-AZ VPC with isolated private subnets for inference nodes, NAT gateways for controlled egress, and a separate management/control subnet for the Redwood control plane peering (customer expects private peering).
- Inbound/outbound: No public inbound allowed to model endpoints. All requests routed through a private API gateway inside customer VPC or via Transit Gateway. Outbound only to approved telemetry endpoints — expect strict allow-listing.
- KMS: customer wants Redwood to support BYOK (bring-your-own-key) via their Azure Key Vault / AWS KMS; key rotation policies and ability to audit key usage are mandatory.
- Audit logging: require >1 year retention for audit events, SIEM integration via Syslog or CloudWatch export. Security asked for example log schema + S3 lifecycle/retention config.
- Data residency: EU-only processing (primary region eu-west-1), with explicit denial of backups to non-EU regions.

POC / timeline:
- POC scope agreed: private VPC + KMS proof-of-concept; run embeddings pipeline and end-to-end audit log shipping to SIEM.
- Milestones: 1) deliver network diagram & required CIDR ranges (this week), 2) finalize security questionnaire answers and sample log exports (2 weeks), 3) set up temporary BYOK test key and run sample inference (POC week).

Quotes / paraphrases from stakeholders:
- Security lead: "We need explicit proofs we can audit every encryption operation and verify keys never leave our control."
- Head of ML infra: "Latency for QA agent must be <120ms p95 for short queries; embeddings throughput peak ~300 qps during nightly ingest windows."

Risks and open questions:
- Legal needs contract clause for EU-only backups — legal still reviewing.
- Unclear whether customer will accept a managed peering (Redwood control plane) or require an out-of-band offline deployment.
- Telemetry egress: need exact FQDNs/IPs to allow-list; requires coordination with network ops.

Suggested next actions for Redwood (AE + SE):
- Ship initial network diagram with proposed CIDR ranges and peering options (Transit Gateway vs VPC peering).
- Provide KMS BYOK integration doc & sample logs (CloudTrail + Syslog) and a short runbook for key rotation audits.
- Book 90-minute architecture workshop with customer infra + security (include Diego, Maya, and solutions architect).
